To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the reliability of fidelity to a family intervention protocol can be enhanced when the coder is provided with the results of a brief ecological assessment, (b) the effect of assessment information on the reliability of ratings of competence was more pronounced when the competence score was calculated as the mean of the ratings of the three competence domains, and (c) the reliability of ratings for each of the three domains of competence was not statistically significantly different between the two conditions.
the reliability of the ratings of fidelity to a family intervention, the Family Check-Up, was significantly higher when the coders had access to assessment data compared to when they did not.
providing assessment data to raters of fidelity improves inter-rater reliability of fidelity ratings, particularly when the quality of the delivery is rated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods to reliably and validly assess therapist adherence to evidence-based practices.
improving the quality of fidelity ratings by providing coders with information about the context in which the intervention is delivered.
the reliability of observational coding of fidelity and competence in family interventions and the role of assessment data in improving these ratings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ecological assessment information enhances the reliability of observational fidelity ratings, and that this enhancement is most pronounced when the fidelity measure includes a rating of therapist competence or quality of implementation.
ecological information improves the reliability of fidelity to the protocol.
ecological assessment data can improve the reliability of ratings of fidelity to assessment-driven interventions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the reliability of ratings of fidelity could be improved by including information about the context in which the intervention is being delivered, particularly for interventions where the context guides intervention selection and delivery.
providing information about the client’s context to the coder improves the reliability of fidelity assessments.
providing coders with assessment information can improve the reliability of fidelity assessments. (author abstract)
The main takeaway from our work is that
fidelity ratings are not always reliable and that the provision of assessment data might be an important step in improving fidelity ratings.
providing assessment information to the coder might improve the reliability of fidelity rating systems, particularly when the quality of intervention delivery is considered.
the validity of ratings of fidelity might be improved by providing coders with assessment information.
